2	name: create-pantoken-app
3	description: Scaffold a new project, or add Instructure design tokens and icons (pantoken) to an existing one. Use when the user wants to start a new app with pantoken already wired in, or wants to add Instructure/Canvas theming, InstUI design tokens, or the pantoken packages to an existing app — detects the framework, installs the right @pantoken/* packages, and wires the token CSS.
4	---
5	
6	# Scaffold pantoken
7	
8	Set up [pantoken](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@pantoken/pantoken) — Instructure UI design tokens and icons —
9	in the current project. Work through these steps.
10	
11	## 1. New project or existing repo?
12	
13	- **Empty directory, or no repo yet** — scaffold a starter with the CLI, then stop (steps 2-3 are
14	  already done for you by the template):
15	
16	  ```sh
17	  npx pantoken-ai scaffold <components|react|vue|svelte|web-components|angular> [--dir .]
18	  ```
19	
20	  This writes a minimal starter (`package.json`, entry file(s), README) for the chosen platform
21	  with pantoken already installed and wired in, and also installs pantoken's agent assets
22	  (AGENTS.md, editor/agent rules, skills) into the same directory. `components` is plain HTML/CSS
23	  (also accepts the alias `html`). If you only want the starter project without the agent assets,
24	  run `npx create-pantoken-app <platform> [--dir .]` (or `npx @pantoken/scaffold <platform>
25	[--dir .]`) directly instead. Run `npm install` (or the detected package manager's install) in
26	  the target directory afterward, substituting `pnpm`/`yarn`/`bun`/`deno` for `npm` as detected. More
27	  platforms land over time; if the desired platform is not yet supported by the scaffold CLI, skip
28	  the CLI entirely and proceed directly to step 2 to manually install and wire pantoken.
29	
30	- **Existing repo you want to add pantoken to** — continue to step 2.
31	
32	## 2. Determine the target
33	
34	Ask the user what kind of project they're building, unless it's unambiguous from the repo. Offer:
35	
36	- **Native web (plain HTML/CSS, no framework) — default** → `@pantoken/components`
37	- A JS framework (React, Vue, Svelte, Angular, React Native, Next.js)
38	- A build tool only, styling from raw tokens (Tailwind, PostCSS, Vite, Webpack, or plain `@pantoken/css`)
39	- A native/CMS ecosystem (Swift, Android, Compose, Flutter, Rust, WordPress, Drupal, Vanilla, Jekyll, Hugo)
40	
41	If the user doesn't answer or has no preference, default to native web (`@pantoken/components`).
42	
43	Corroborate with the repo when possible, and prefer the user's answer if it conflicts with detection:
44	
45	- `package.json` dependencies → web framework (react, vue, svelte, @angular/core, react-native,
46	  next, vite, tailwindcss, webpack, postcss).
47	- If no `package.json` is found and the user wants a web project, run `npm init -y` first, then
48	  proceed with the native web default (or the chosen framework).
49	- Native project files → iOS (`Package.swift`, `*.xcodeproj`), Android (`build.gradle`), Flutter
50	  (`pubspec.yaml`), WordPress/Drupal/Vanilla theme dirs.
51	
52	Also detect the package manager from the lockfile present in the repo, and use its equivalent
53	command for every install/run step below instead of assuming npm:
54	
55	| Lockfile found             | Package manager | Add package(s)       | Run a package's CLI  |
56	| -------------------------- | --------------- | -------------------- | -------------------- |
57	| `pnpm-lock.yaml`           | pnpm            | `pnpm add <pkg>`     | `pnpm dlx <pkg>`     |
58	| `yarn.lock`                | yarn            | `yarn add <pkg>`     | `yarn dlx <pkg>`     |
59	| `bun.lock`/`bun.lockb`     | bun             | `bun add <pkg>`      | `bunx <pkg>`         |
60	| `deno.lock`                | deno            | `deno add npm:<pkg>` | `deno run npm:<pkg>` |
61	| `package-lock.json` / none | npm             | `npm i <pkg>`        | `npx <pkg>`          |
62	
63	If no lockfile exists yet, default to npm (or whatever the user prefers).
64	
65	## 3. Install
66	
67	Use the package manager detected in step 2 for every command below (the examples use `npm i`;
68	substitute `pnpm add`, `yarn add`, or `bun add` as appropriate).
69	
70	Follow this decision checklist in order:
71	
72	1. **Is it native web** (plain HTML/CSS, no framework and no build tool detected)? Install only
73	   `@pantoken/components` — it ships the token CSS baked in, so no separate `@pantoken/css` install
74	   is needed — and stop:
75	
76	   ```sh
77	   npm i @pantoken/components
78	   ```
79	
80	2. **Is it Next.js?** Install `@pantoken/css` plus `@pantoken/next` (do NOT also install
81	   `@pantoken/react` — `@pantoken/next` includes the React integration), then add any matching tool
82	   packages (Tailwind, Vite, etc.) from the table below.
83	
84	3. **Otherwise**, install `@pantoken/css` first:
85	
86	   ```sh
87	   npm i @pantoken/css
88	   ```
89	
90	   Then add the framework package and every matching tool row's package from the table. Framework
91	   rows (React, Vue, etc.) and tool rows (Tailwind, PostCSS, Vite, Webpack) are all additive —
92	   install every matching row's package alongside `@pantoken/css`.
93	
94	For example:
95	
96	- A Next.js project also using Tailwind installs `@pantoken/css @pantoken/next @pantoken/tailwind`.
97	- A React project also using Vite installs `@pantoken/css @pantoken/react @pantoken/vite`.
98	
99	| Detected                | Install                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
100	| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
101	| Native web (default)    | `@pantoken/components`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
102	| React                   | `@pantoken/react`; if the user also wants full InstUI components (buttons, modals, etc.), additionally install the specific `@instructure/ui-*` packages needed, e.g. `@instructure/ui-buttons @instructure/ui-modal` (see <https://instructure.design> for the full package list) |
103	| Vue / Svelte / Angular  | `@pantoken/vue` / `@pantoken/svelte` / `@pantoken/angular` + `@pantoken/web-components` (always install `@pantoken/web-components` alongside the framework package — it's required for icon support, not optional)                                                                 |
104	| React Native            | `@pantoken/react-native`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
105	| Next.js                 | `@pantoken/next` — Next.js projects do NOT also need `@pantoken/react`; `@pantoken/next` includes the React integration. Do not install both.                                                                                                                                      |
106	| Vite                    | `@pantoken/vite`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
107	| Tailwind                | `@pantoken/tailwind`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
108	| PostCSS / Webpack       | `@pantoken/postcss` / `@pantoken/webpack`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
109	| shadcn / Bootstrap      | `@pantoken/shadcn` / `@pantoken/bootstrap`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
110	| markdown-it / css-in-js | `@pantoken/markdown-it` / `@pantoken/css-in-js`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
111	| Icons anywhere          | `@pantoken/web-components`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
112	
113	For native / CMS targets, no install — run the CLI (step 5).
114	
115	## 4. Wire it up
116	
117	- Native web (default): import `base.css` + `components.css` from `@pantoken/components` (e.g.
118	  `import "@pantoken/components/base.css"; import "@pantoken/components/components.css";`), then
119	  apply classes like `class="instui-button"` to markup.
120	- Other web entry: add `import "@pantoken/css/inject";` (or `@import "@pantoken/css/style.css";`).
121	- Next: wrap the config with `withPantoken(...)` and import the CSS in the root layout.
122	- Vite: add the `pantoken()` plugin. Tailwind: add `pantokenPreset()` to `presets`.
123	- Web components: `import "@pantoken/web-components";` then use `<instui-icon name="…">`.
124	- Verify the app renders and `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--instui-color-background-brand')` is non-empty.
125	  If the property is empty, check that the token CSS import (`@pantoken/components/base.css` or
126	  `@pantoken/css/inject`) appears before any component imports in the entry file, and that the dev
127	  server was restarted after install. Report the specific failure to the user with corrective steps.
128	
129	## 5. Native / other ecosystems
130	
131	```sh
132	npx pantoken generate <swift|android|compose|flutter|rust|wordpress|vanilla|drupal|jekyll|hugo> --out <dir> [--icons a,b] [--theme rebrand]
133	```
134	
135	Substitute `pnpm dlx`, `yarn dlx`, `bunx`, or `deno run npm:` for `npx` per the package manager detected in step 1.
136	
137	## Conventions to follow afterward
138	
139	- Style with `var(--instui-*)` references, not hard-coded colours, so light/dark and high-contrast
140	  theming keeps working.
141	- Resolve real token names from `@pantoken/tokens`; never invent them.

# Init pantoken (AI assets)

Install pantoken's consumer-facing agent assets into the current repo: `AGENTS.md`, `llms.txt`,
editor/agent rule files (Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf), and the `scaffold-pantoken` skill.

```sh
npx pantoken-ai init
```

This installs every asset by default. To scope it to one tool, pass
`--tool <agents|llms|cursor|copilot|windsurf|claude>`. To target a directory other than the
current one, pass `--dir <path>`. Substitute `pnpm dlx`, `yarn dlx`, `bunx`, or `deno run npm:` for `npx` depending
on the package manager detected in the repo (look for `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, or
`bun.lock`/`bun.lockb`; default to npm/npx if none is found).

That's all this skill does — it only writes the asset files above, it does not install any
`@pantoken/*` package or modify application code. Once the assets are installed, use the
`scaffold-pantoken` skill (or run `npx pantoken-ai scaffold <platform>` directly) to scaffold a
new project or wire pantoken into an existing one.

1	# Working with pantoken (Instructure design tokens & icons)
2	
3	This project uses **pantoken** to consume Instructure UI design tokens and icons. pantoken exports
4	the resolved tokens once and re-shapes them for many platforms. Reach for the smallest scoped
5	package that fits the task (e.g. `@pantoken/components`, `@pantoken/css`, `@pantoken/tokens`). The
6	unified `pantoken` package re-exports all scoped packages; only install it with
7	`npm i @pantoken/pantoken` when you need several of those packages together in one dependency.
8	
9	## The token model
10	
11	Tokens are CSS custom properties named `--instui-<group>-<name>` (e.g.
12	`--instui-color-background-brand`, `--instui-spacing-space-md`). Themes: `rebrand` (default, with
13	`light-dark()` where light ≠ dark), `canvas`, `canvasHighContrast`. Icons are `<image>` tokens
14	(`--instui-icon-<name>`) derived from Lucide + Instructure custom glyphs.
15	
16	To activate a non-default theme, pass `--theme canvas` to the CLI or use `byTheme("canvas")` from
17	`@pantoken/tokens`. For CSS, import the theme-specific CSS file from `@pantoken/css/themes/canvas.css`.
18	To scope a theme to a subtree rather than the whole page, wrap that subtree in an element and apply
19	the theme CSS file or `byTheme()` output scoped to that element's selector. Nested theming is not
20	supported out of the box; each theme CSS file sets vars at `:root`.
21	
22	## Pick the right package
23	
24	**Decision order for web styling** — pick the first that matches:
25	
26	1. Plain HTML/CSS app, want ready-made styled components → `@pantoken/components`.
27	2. Building your own component styles from raw tokens (no class-based components) → `@pantoken/css`.
28	3. Need token values in JS/TS logic (not just CSS) → `@pantoken/tokens`.
29	4. Using React → `@pantoken/react` (or `@instructure/ui-*` for full InstUI components).
30	5. Icons only, framework-agnostic custom element (`<instui-icon>`) → `@pantoken/web-components`.
31	   For raw decoded SVG markup/data instead of a custom element, use `@pantoken/icons` (`getIcon("arrow-left")`).
32	
33	After selecting a base package, also consider `@pantoken/plugin-layouts` (app-shell layout) and
34	`@pantoken/plugin-custom-components` (extra components) when using `@pantoken/components`.
35	
36	**Web (CSS / JS):**
37	
38	- `@pantoken/components` — **preferred bootstrap for plain HTML/CSS web apps.** The InstUI-look
39	  class-based component library (`components.css`: `.instui-button`, `.instui-alert`, `.instui-badge`,
40	  …), plus `base.css` (document defaults + focus ring), `prose.css` (content/markdown styling),
41	  `utilities.css` (spacing/layout/colour utility classes), `icons.css`, and opt-in `fonts.css` /
42	  `select.css`. Built from the tokens with no InstUI React dependency.
43	- `@pantoken/plugin-layouts` — layout composition records (currently `wrapper`) that compose
44	  `@pantoken/components` into an app-shell structure. Use alongside `@pantoken/components` when
45	  bootstrapping a full page layout.
46	- `@pantoken/plugin-custom-components` — additional cssdoc-documented components beyond the core set
47	  (currently `card`, `banner`, `agent-shell`). Use alongside `@pantoken/components` for extra component patterns.
48	- `@pantoken/css` — all tokens emitted as `--instui-*` CSS custom-property (`var()`) declarations, with
49	  no class-based components. `import "@pantoken/css/inject"` (side-effect) or
50	  `import { css } from "@pantoken/css"`. Reach for this when you're building your own component styles
51	  from the raw tokens rather than using `@pantoken/components`.
52	- `@pantoken/tokens` — the resolved token IR as JS/TS (`import { tokens, byTheme } from "@pantoken/tokens"`).
53	- `@pantoken/icons` — decoded SVG icon set as raw markup/data (`getIcon("arrow-left")`). Use when you
54	  need the SVG itself (e.g. to inline, transform, or feed to another rendering system) rather than a
55	  ready-made element.
56	- `@pantoken/interactions` — vanilla JS behavior functions for components (modal, tooltip, in-place-edit, close-button). IIFE entry points for CDN consumers; ESM for bundlers.
57	- `@pantoken/web-components` — `<instui-icon name="arrow-left">` + styled primitives. Framework-agnostic.
58	  Prefer this for drop-in icon markup; it renders `@pantoken/icons` under the hood as a custom element.
59	
60	**Frameworks:**
61	
62	- React: `@pantoken/react` (`<Icon>`, `useToken`, `TokenProvider`). For InstUI's full React components use `@instructure/ui-*`.
63	- Vue: `@pantoken/vue` (plugin). Svelte: `@pantoken/svelte` (`icon` action). Angular: `@pantoken/angular`.
64	- React Native: `@pantoken/react-native` (StyleSheet-friendly objects, no CSS vars).
65	- Markdown: `@pantoken/react-markdown` (react-markdown → InstUI), `@pantoken/rehype` (`:icon:` tokens).
66	
67	**Build tools:**
68	
69	- Vite: `@pantoken/vite` (virtual modules + CSS inject). Next: `@pantoken/next` (`withPantoken` for `transpilePackages`).
70	- Tailwind: `@pantoken/tailwind` (preset → `bg-color-background-base`). PostCSS: `@pantoken/postcss` (`@pantoken;` at-rule). Webpack: `@pantoken/webpack`.
71	
72	**Theme other systems:** `@pantoken/shadcn`, `@pantoken/bootstrap` (CSS-var bridges), `@pantoken/storybook` (theme).
73	
74	**Native / other ecosystems (generated via CLI):** `pantoken generate <target>` where target is
75	`swift`, `android`, `compose`, `flutter`, `rust`, `wordpress`, `vanilla`, `drupal`, `jekyll`, or
76	`hugo`. Add `--icons a,b` to also emit icon assets, `--theme <name>`, `--out <dir>`, and for Rust
77	`--format <egui|iced>`.
78	
79	**Design & interchange:** `@pantoken/dtcg` (W3C DTCG JSON), `@pantoken/scss` (SCSS vars),
80	`@pantoken/figma` (Figma Variables payload), `@pantoken/email` (inline-friendly values).
81	
82	## Common recipes
83	
84	- **Bootstrap a plain web app:** `npm i @pantoken/components` then import `base.css` +
85	  `components.css` (+ `utilities.css` as needed). Apply classes like `class="instui-button"` to your
86	  markup. Add `@pantoken/plugin-layouts` for an app-shell layout and
87	  `@pantoken/plugin-custom-components` for extra components (`card`, `banner`, `agent-shell`).
88	- **Style from raw tokens only (no components):** `npm i @pantoken/css` then
89	  `import "@pantoken/css/inject";`. Use `var(--instui-color-background-brand)` etc. in your own CSS.
90	- **Icons anywhere:** `npm i @pantoken/web-components`, `import "@pantoken/web-components";`, then
91	  `<instui-icon name="check-mark"></instui-icon>`.
92	- **Component behaviors (vanilla JS):** `npm i @pantoken/interactions`, then import `initModal`, `initTooltip`, `initInPlaceEdit`, or `initCloseButton` to wire behaviors. For CDN/IIFE: link `@pantoken/interactions/dist/interactions.iife.js` and check `component-capabilities.json` for per-component `.iife.js` entry points.
93	- **Tailwind:** add `pantokenPreset()` to `presets` and import `@pantoken/css`.
94	- **Native app:** `npx pantoken generate swift --out ./ios/Tokens --icons arrow-left,check-mark`.
95	- **Rust app:** `npx pantoken generate rust --out ./src/tokens.rs --format egui`.
96	- **Push to Figma:** `toFigmaVariables(tokens)` → feed a Figma plugin / the Variables REST API.
97	
98	## IDE integration
99	
100	- **Class/token completion:** `npm i @pantoken/pantoken`, then point VS Code at its shipped
101	  custom-data JSON in workspace `.vscode/settings.json`:
102	
103	  ```json
104	  {
105	    "html.customData": ["./node_modules/@pantoken/pantoken/dist/html-custom-data.json"],
106	    "css.customData": ["./node_modules/@pantoken/pantoken/dist/css-custom-data.json"]
107	  }
108	  ```
109	
110	  Reload VS Code to pick up the new data. This gives completion/hover for `instui-*` classes
111	  (and `-modifier` class tokens) and `--instui-*` custom properties without a pantoken-specific
112	  extension.
113	
114	- **cssdoc authoring support:** install the `cssdoc.cssdoc-vscode` extension for hover/completion
115	  on cssdoc doc-comment tags (`@component`, `@token`, `@affects`, etc.) when authoring or reading
116	  the `.css` records that back `@pantoken/components` and its plugins.
117	
118	## Full documentation
119	
120	This file is a cheatsheet and can lag behind the real API surface. For anything it doesn't cover, or
121	to confirm a detail, fetch the live docs at `https://pantoken.iywahl.com/`:
122	
123	- `/llms.txt` — an agent-legible index of the whole site.
124	- `/llms-full.txt` — the entire site as one document.
125	- Any page as Markdown by appending `.md` to its URL (e.g. `/guide/packages.md`).
126	- `/.well-known/api-catalog` — a machine-readable manifest linking to the above.
127	
128	## Rules
129	
130	- Prefer `var(--instui-*)` references over hard-coded colours so theming (light/dark, high-contrast) keeps working.
131	- Don't invent token names — resolve them from `@pantoken/tokens` or the generated CSS.
132	- To discover available tokens, import `tokens` from `@pantoken/tokens` and inspect its keys, or open the generated CSS file and search for `--instui-`.
133	- For non-React frameworks that lack a dedicated pantoken package, prefer `@pantoken/web-components`
134	  over porting components. When a framework package exists (Vue, Svelte, Angular), use it instead.

# Scaffold pantoken

Set up [pantoken](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@pantoken/pantoken) — Instructure UI design tokens and icons —
in the current project. Work through these steps.

## 1. New project or existing repo?

- **Empty directory, or no repo yet** — scaffold a starter with the CLI, then stop (steps 2-3 are
  already done for you by the template):

  ```sh
  npx pantoken-ai scaffold <components|react|vue|svelte|web-components|angular> [--dir .]
  ```

  This writes a minimal starter (`package.json`, entry file(s), README) for the chosen platform
  with pantoken already installed and wired in, and also installs pantoken's agent assets
  (AGENTS.md, editor/agent rules, skills) into the same directory. `components` is plain HTML/CSS
  (also accepts the alias `html`). If you only want the starter project without the agent assets,
  run `npx create-pantoken-app <platform> [--dir .]` (or `npx @pantoken/scaffold <platform>
[--dir .]`) directly instead. Run `npm install` (or the detected package manager's install) in
  the target directory afterward, substituting `pnpm`/`yarn`/`bun` for `npm` as detected. More
  platforms land over time; if the desired platform is not yet supported by the scaffold CLI, skip
  the CLI entirely and proceed directly to step 2 to manually install and wire pantoken.

- **Existing repo you want to add pantoken to** — continue to step 2.

## 2. Determine the target

Ask the user what kind of project they're building, unless it's unambiguous from the repo. Offer:

- **Native web (plain HTML/CSS, no framework) — default** → `@pantoken/components`
- A JS framework (React, Vue, Svelte, Angular, React Native, Next.js)
- A build tool only, styling from raw tokens (Tailwind, PostCSS, Vite, Webpack, or plain `@pantoken/css`)
- A native/CMS ecosystem (Swift, Android, Compose, Flutter, Rust, WordPress, Drupal, Vanilla, Jekyll, Hugo)

If the user doesn't answer or has no preference, default to native web (`@pantoken/components`).

Corroborate with the repo when possible, and prefer the user's answer if it conflicts with detection:

- `package.json` dependencies → web framework (react, vue, svelte, @angular/core, react-native,
  next, vite, tailwindcss, webpack, postcss).
- If no `package.json` is found and the user wants a web project, run `npm init -y` first, then
  proceed with the native web default (or the chosen framework).
- Native project files → iOS (`Package.swift`, `*.xcodeproj`), Android (`build.gradle`), Flutter
  (`pubspec.yaml`), WordPress/Drupal/Vanilla theme dirs.

Also detect the package manager from the lockfile present in the repo, and use its equivalent
command for every install/run step below instead of assuming npm:

| Lockfile found             | Package manager | Add package(s)   | Run a package's CLI |
| -------------------------- | --------------- | ---------------- | ------------------- |
| `pnpm-lock.yaml`           | pnpm            | `pnpm add <pkg>` | `pnpm dlx <pkg>`    |
| `yarn.lock`                | yarn            | `yarn add <pkg>` | `yarn dlx <pkg>`    |
| `bun.lock`/`bun.lockb`     | bun             | `bun add <pkg>`  | `bunx <pkg>`        |
| `package-lock.json` / none | npm             | `npm i <pkg>`    | `npx <pkg>`         |

If no lockfile exists yet, default to npm (or whatever the user prefers).

## 3. Install

Use the package manager detected in step 2 for every command below (the examples use `npm i`;
substitute `pnpm add`, `yarn add`, or `bun add` as appropriate).

Follow this decision checklist in order:

1. **Is it native web** (plain HTML/CSS, no framework and no build tool detected)? Install only
   `@pantoken/components` — it ships the token CSS baked in, so no separate `@pantoken/css` install
   is needed — and stop:

   ```sh
   npm i @pantoken/components
   ```

2. **Is it Next.js?** Install `@pantoken/css` plus `@pantoken/next` (do NOT also install
   `@pantoken/react` — `@pantoken/next` includes the React integration), then add any matching tool
   packages (Tailwind, Vite, etc.) from the table below.

3. **Otherwise**, install `@pantoken/css` first:

   ```sh
   npm i @pantoken/css
   ```

   Then add the framework package and every matching tool row's package from the table. Framework
   rows (React, Vue, etc.) and tool rows (Tailwind, PostCSS, Vite, Webpack) are all additive —
   install every matching row's package alongside `@pantoken/css`.

For example:

- A Next.js project also using Tailwind installs `@pantoken/css @pantoken/next @pantoken/tailwind`.
- A React project also using Vite installs `@pantoken/css @pantoken/react @pantoken/vite`.

| Native web (default)    | `@pantoken/components`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| React                   | `@pantoken/react`; if the user also wants full InstUI components (buttons, modals, etc.), additionally install the specific `@instructure/ui-*` packages needed, e.g. `@instructure/ui-buttons @instructure/ui-modal` (see <https://instructure.design> for the full package list) |

| Next.js                 | `@pantoken/next` — Next.js projects do NOT also need `@pantoken/react`; `@pantoken/next` includes the React integration. | Vite                    | `@pantoken/vite`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Tailwind                | `@pantoken/tailwind`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| PostCSS / Webpack       | `@pantoken/postcss` / `@pantoken/webpack`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| shadcn / Bootstrap      | `@pantoken/shadcn` / `@pantoken/bootstrap`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| markdown-it / css-in-js | `@pantoken/markdown-it` / `@pantoken/css-in-js`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Icons anywhere          | `@pantoken/web-components`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

For native / CMS targets, no install — run the CLI (step 5).

## 4. Wire it up

- Native web (default): import `base.css` + `components.css` from `@pantoken/components` (e.g.
  `import "@pantoken/components/base.css"; import "@pantoken/components/components.css";`), then
  apply classes like `class="instui-button"` to markup.
- Other web entry: add `import "@pantoken/css/inject";` (or `@import "@pantoken/css/style.css";`).
- Next: wrap the config with `withPantoken(...)` and import the CSS in the root layout.
- Vite: add the `pantoken()` plugin. Tailwind: add `pantokenPreset()` to `presets`.
- Web components: `import "@pantoken/web-components";` then use `<instui-icon name="…">`.
- Verify the app renders and `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--instui-color-background-brand')` is non-empty.
  If the property is empty, check that the token CSS import (`@pantoken/components/base.css` or
  `@pantoken/css/inject`) appears before any component imports in the entry file, and that the dev
  server was restarted after install. Report the specific failure to the user with corrective steps.

## 5. Native / other ecosystems

```sh
npx pantoken generate <swift|android|compose|flutter|rust|wordpress|vanilla|drupal|jekyll|hugo> --out <dir> [--icons a,b] [--theme rebrand]
```

Substitute `pnpm dlx`, `yarn dlx`, or `bunx` for `npx` per the package manager detected in step 1.

## Conventions to follow afterward

- Style with `var(--instui-*)` references, not hard-coded colours, so light/dark and high-contrast
  theming keeps working.
- Resolve real token names from `@pantoken/tokens`; never invent them.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Claude Code CLI non-interactive mode, the print flag, and related features:

## Non-Interactive Mode (Headless)

Add the -p (or --print) flag to any claude command to run it non-interactively. It runs Claude Code with a prompt, outputs to stdout, and exits. No interactive session.

## The Print Flag

--print (or -p) is the core headless flag. It sends one prompt, prints the result to standard output, and exits with a status code, so scripts, cron jobs, and CI/CD pipelines can drive Claude Code without a human at the terminal.

## Slash Commands and Skills in Headless Mode

Important limitation: slash commands/skills are interactive-mode only — there's no claude -c '/pr-msg' equivalent. In -p (prompt) mode, skills aren't loaded. User-invoked skills like /code-review are unavailable headlessly: those commands belong to the interactive shell, so inside automation you describe the task you want done instead.

## Permissions in Headless Mode

You'll typically need the --dangerously-skip-permissions flag for headless runs, which should be used carefully and only for well-tested skills. For fully non-interactive runs you need to combine --print with permission flags.

Based on the search results, here's what you need to know about the Gemini CLI `--yolo` flag and headless mode:

## The `--yolo` Flag

The `--yolo` flag enables YOLO mode, which automatically approves all tool calls. In YOLO mode, as soon as the AI decides on a tool (like running a shell command or writing to a file), it executes it immediately, without that "Approve? (y/n)" prompt.

## Using `--yolo` in Headless Mode

You can run Gemini CLI headless with `--yolo` in a completely automated script or CI pipeline so it doesn't pause for confirmation. This combination is particularly useful for unattended operation in automated workflows.

## Important Security Warning

The `--yolo` flag auto-approves all tool executions including shell commands. You should avoid `--yolo` in untrusted contexts.

## Alternative Approval Modes

If you want more granular control, there are approval modes available: `default` (prompt for approval on each tool call), `auto_edit` (automatically approve edit tools while prompting for others), and `yolo` (automatically approve all tool calls).

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the gemini-cli positional prompt argument and interactive sessions:

## Positional Prompt Argument Behavior

The Gemini CLI accepts a prompt as a positional argument (e.g., `gemini "my prompt"`), which boots Gemini CLI into interactive mode with the initial prompt. The positional prompt defaults to interactive mode in a TTY.

## Issues with Other Flags

There's a known issue with how positional prompts interact with other flags. When providing a prompt as a positional argument along with other flags (e.g., `gemini -e none "Hello, world!"`), the Gemini CLI ignores the positional prompt and enters interactive mode. It displays the Gemini logo and does not process the prompt.

## Non-Interactive Execution

Use -p/--prompt for non-interactive execution. However, the positional prompt is now the preferred way to invoke the gemini command directly and without the terminal interface.

## Additional Context

The CLI accepts a positional prompt together with --prompt-interactive, even though both provide the initial prompt. This creates conflicts in how the CLI handles the input depending on whether it's running in interactive or headless mode.

# Fix the create-pantoken-app rename and ship a working Claude/Gemini bootstrap one-liner

## Context

You asked what the modern (2026) way is to hand someone a one-liner that installs pantoken's
agent assets and kicks off the `create-pantoken-app` skill, for someone using either the Claude
Code CLI or the Gemini CLI.

While digging in, I found two things that make this more than a documentation question:

1. **The `scaffold-pantoken` → `create-pantoken-app` skill rename is only half-done.** The skill's
   source directory was renamed on disk (`ai/pantoken-ai/skills/create-pantoken-app/` exists,
   `skills/scaffold-pantoken/` is deleted per `git status`), but every place that *reads* or
   *installs* that skill still points at the old name: the asset generator, the installed file
   path, the test suite, the README, and the docs site. Right now `npx @pantoken/ai init` would
   fail (it reads a `skills/scaffold-pantoken/SKILL.md` file that no longer exists), so no
   Claude one-liner can work until this is finished.
2. **The docs site's "Get started" terminal widget (`GetStartedTabs.vue`) already has an in-progress
   "ai" tab meant to be exactly this one-liner — and its command construction is broken.** The `ai`
   pm option hardcodes a `"claude "` launcher prefix *and* derives a base command that already
   contains its own `claude`-invoking text, so the rendered/copyable command would literally read
   `claude npx @pantoken/ai init && /scaffold-pantoken` — which is not valid shell (the unquoted
   `&&` is interpreted by the outer shell, not passed to `claude`, and `/scaffold-pantoken` would
   run as a nonexistent command) and duplicates `claude`.

So the plan is: finish the rename, fix the widget's command construction so it produces one valid,
copy-pasteable shell command, and add the Gemini CLI equivalent you asked for.

## The recommended one-liners

Verified against the current (Aug 2026) Claude Code and Gemini CLI docs/behavior:

- **Claude Code CLI:** slash commands/skills only work in Claude's *interactive* mode, not
  headless `-p` mode — so the one-liner has to launch an interactive session with the skill
  invocation as the first message, exactly like typing it by hand:

  ```sh
  npx @pantoken/ai init && claude "/create-pantoken-app"
  ```

  `claude "<text>"` (no `-p`) boots the normal interactive REPL with `<text>` as the first turn, so
  the slash command is parsed and the skill runs with normal tool-approval prompts.

- **Gemini CLI:** Gemini has no packaged "skill" format for pantoken today (no `--tool gemini` in
  `@pantoken/ai`'s installer), but Gemini CLI *does* support the same "positional prompt boots an
  interactive session" behavior as Claude (`gemini "<text>"` in a TTY defaults to interactive mode
  with that as the first message — confirmed in the Gemini CLI docs; `-p`/`--prompt` is the
  separate *headless*, no-approval-prompt path and isn't what we want for a first-try demo). Since
  there's no skill to invoke, point it at the AGENTS.md file `init` just installed instead:

  ```sh
  npx @pantoken/ai init && gemini "Read AGENTS.md and follow it to set up pantoken in this project."
  ```

  This is deliberately asymmetric with Claude: Claude gets the full structured `create-pantoken-app`
  skill; Gemini gets the same underlying guidance via the tool-agnostic `AGENTS.md` cheatsheet,
  since pantoken doesn't ship a Gemini extension. Both stay interactive (no `-p`/`--yolo`), so the
  user sees and approves every install/file-write step, matching Claude's flow.

## Changes

### 1. Finish the `scaffold-pantoken` → `create-pantoken-app` rename

- [ai/pantoken-ai/scripts/generate.ts](ai/pantoken-ai/scripts/generate.ts) — read from
  `skills/create-pantoken-app/SKILL.md` instead of the deleted `skills/scaffold-pantoken/SKILL.md`.
  Rename the `scaffoldSkill` asset key to `createAppSkill` (it's read in the two places below).
- [ai/pantoken-ai/generated/assets.ts](ai/pantoken-ai/generated/assets.ts) — regenerate (run the
  package's `generate` script) rather than hand-edit; it's build output.
- [ai/pantoken-ai/src/index.ts](ai/pantoken-ai/src/index.ts) — in `TARGETS.claude`, write to
  `.claude/skills/create-pantoken-app/SKILL.md` using `ASSETS.createAppSkill`; update the module
  doc comment's skill list (`init-pantoken`, `create-pantoken-app`).
- [ai/pantoken-ai/tests/index.test.ts](ai/pantoken-ai/tests/index.test.ts) — update the assertion
  path from `.claude/skills/scaffold-pantoken/SKILL.md` to
  `.claude/skills/create-pantoken-app/SKILL.md`.
- [ai/pantoken-ai/skills/init-pantoken/SKILL.md](ai/pantoken-ai/skills/init-pantoken/SKILL.md) —
  the two mentions of "the `scaffold-pantoken` skill" → "the `create-pantoken-app` skill".
- [ai/pantoken-ai/README.md](ai/pantoken-ai/README.md) — both `scaffold-pantoken` mentions →
  `create-pantoken-app`.
- [ai/pantoken-ai/package.json](ai/pantoken-ai/package.json) — `description` field: "init-pantoken/
  scaffold-pantoken Claude Code skills" → "init-pantoken/create-pantoken-app Claude Code skills".
- [docs/guide/getting-started.md](docs/guide/getting-started.md) — `` /scaffold-pantoken `` →
  `` /create-pantoken-app ``.
- Leave `CHANGELOG.md` entries and `.changeset/scaffold-cli-deno-support.md` alone — they're
  historical release notes describing what was true at the time, not living docs.
- Don't hand-edit `docs/api/ai/pantoken-ai/src/index.md`, its `hu` counterpart, or the
  `docs/i18n-cache/*.json` files — they're generated (typedoc + translation cache) and will fall
  back into sync the next time the docs build / translation script runs. Flag this as a follow-up
  rather than doing it by hand now.
- `docs/hu/guide/getting-started.md` is also translation-pipeline output — update the English
  source only; regenerate the Hungarian guide via the existing translate script rather than
  hand-editing.

### 2. Fix and extend the docs "Get started" terminal widget

- [docs/.vitepress/theme/get-started.ts](docs/.vitepress/theme/get-started.ts) — rename
  `aiCommand` → `claudeCommand`, update its text to reference the correct skill name and the
  quoted `claude` invocation, and add a new `geminiCommand` default:

  ```ts
  claudeCommand:
    'Run `npx @pantoken/ai init` in this repo, then run `claude "/create-pantoken-app"`.',
  geminiCommand:
    'Run `npx @pantoken/ai init` in this repo, then run `gemini "Read AGENTS.md and follow it to set up pantoken in this project."`.',
  ```

  (Extracting the backtick-delimited code spans and joining with `&&`, as the widget already does,
  yields exactly the two one-liners above.)

- [docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts](docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts) — same rename in both the `en` and `hu`
  locale overrides (translate the `hu` copy analogous to its existing style).

- [docs/.vitepress/theme/components/GetStartedTabs.vue](docs/.vitepress/theme/components/GetStartedTabs.vue):
  - Rename the `"ai"` pm option's `id`/`label` to `"claude"` (now that there'll be two AI-CLI
    entries, "ai" alone is ambiguous) and set its `launcher` to `""` — the derived command already
    contains the `claude "..."` invocation, so the old hardcoded `"claude "` launcher prefix was
    causing the duplicate/invalid command described above.
  - Add a new `gemini` pm option: `{ id: "gemini", label: "gemini", launcher: "", color: "#8E75B2",
    icon: "googlegemini" }` (hex verified against `simple-icons`' own data for "Google Gemini").
  - Extend `baseCommandFor` to special-case `"claude"` → `deriveInlineCommand(getStartedTabs.value.claudeCommand)`
    and `"gemini"` → `deriveInlineCommand(getStartedTabs.value.geminiCommand)` (rename
    `deriveAiInlineCommand`/`FALLBACK_AI_INLINE_COMMAND` accordingly, and give the fallback a
    gemini counterpart).
  - Add `@import "@pantoken/plugin-simple-icons/icons/googlegemini.css";` alongside the other icon
    imports in the `<style>` block (`@pantoken/plugin-simple-icons` is already a `docs` dependency).

### 3. Changeset

Per this repo's convention, add a changeset (`pnpm changeset`) covering both packages touched:
`@pantoken/ai` (the rename completion) and the docs site (the fixed/extended get-started widget).

## Verification

- `ai/pantoken-ai`: run its test suite (`vpr test` in that package) — confirms `npx @pantoken/ai
  init` once again writes a real, existing skill file, and the renamed path assertion passes.
- Regenerate `ai/pantoken-ai/generated/assets.ts` and confirm `ASSETS.createAppSkill` contains the
  current `create-pantoken-app/SKILL.md` content (not the deleted scaffold-pantoken text).
- Docs site: start the docs dev server, open the "Get started" page, and step through the pm
  picker — confirm the `claude` and `gemini` entries each render one syntactically valid,
  copy-pastable single-line shell command (no duplicated `claude`, no bare `&&`-split commands),
  and that "Copy" copies exactly that line.
- Sanity-check the two recommended commands by hand: `npx @pantoken/ai init && claude

# Fix the create-pantoken-app rename and ship a working Claude/Gemini bootstrap one-liner

## Context

You asked what the modern (2026) way is to hand someone a one-liner that installs pantoken's
agent assets and kicks off the `create-pantoken-app` skill, for someone using either the Claude
Code CLI or the Gemini CLI.

While digging in, I found two things that make this more than a documentation question:

1. **The `scaffold-pantoken` → `create-pantoken-app` skill rename is only half-done.** The skill's
   source directory was renamed on disk (`ai/pantoken-ai/skills/create-pantoken-app/` exists,
   `skills/scaffold-pantoken/` is deleted per `git status`), but every place that *reads* or
   *installs* that skill still points at the old name: the asset generator, the installed file
   path, the test suite, the README, and the docs site. Right now `npx @pantoken/ai init` would
   fail (it reads a `skills/scaffold-pantoken/SKILL.md` file that no longer exists), so no
   Claude one-liner can work until this is finished.
2. **The docs site's "Get started" terminal widget (`GetStartedTabs.vue`) already has an in-progress
   "ai" tab meant to be exactly this one-liner — and its command construction is broken.** The `ai`
   pm option hardcodes a `"claude "` launcher prefix *and* derives a base command that already
   contains its own `claude`-invoking text, so the rendered/copyable command would literally read
   `claude npx @pantoken/ai init && /scaffold-pantoken` — which is not valid shell (the unquoted
   `&&` is interpreted by the outer shell, not passed to `claude`, and `/scaffold-pantoken` would
   run as a nonexistent command) and duplicates `claude`.

So the plan is: finish the rename, fix the widget's command construction so it produces one valid,
copy-pasteable shell command, and add the Gemini CLI equivalent you asked for.

## The recommended one-liners

Verified against the current (Aug 2026) Claude Code and Gemini CLI docs/behavior:

- **Claude Code CLI:** slash commands/skills only work in Claude's *interactive* mode, not
  headless `-p` mode — so the one-liner has to launch an interactive session with the skill
  invocation as the first message, exactly like typing it by hand:

  ```sh
  npx @pantoken/ai init && claude "/create-pantoken-app"
  ```

  `claude "<text>"` (no `-p`) boots the normal interactive REPL with `<text>` as the first turn, so
  the slash command is parsed and the skill runs with normal tool-approval prompts.

- **Gemini CLI:** Gemini has no packaged "skill" format for pantoken today (no `--tool gemini` in
  `@pantoken/ai`'s installer), but Gemini CLI *does* support the same "positional prompt boots an
  interactive session" behavior as Claude (`gemini "<text>"` in a TTY defaults to interactive mode
  with that as the first message — confirmed in the Gemini CLI docs; `-p`/`--prompt` is the
  separate *headless*, no-approval-prompt path and isn't what we want for a first-try demo). Since
  there's no skill to invoke, point it at the AGENTS.md file `init` just installed instead:

  ```sh
  npx @pantoken/ai init && gemini "Read AGENTS.md and follow it to set up pantoken in this project."
  ```

  This is deliberately asymmetric with Claude: Claude gets the full structured `create-pantoken-app`
  skill; Gemini gets the same underlying guidance via the tool-agnostic `AGENTS.md` cheatsheet,
  since pantoken doesn't ship a Gemini extension. Both stay interactive (no `-p`/`--yolo`), so the
  user sees and approves every install/file-write step, matching Claude's flow.

## Changes

### 1. Finish the `scaffold-pantoken` → `create-pantoken-app` rename

- [ai/pantoken-ai/scripts/generate.ts](ai/pantoken-ai/scripts/generate.ts) — read from
  `skills/create-pantoken-app/SKILL.md` instead of the deleted `skills/scaffold-pantoken/SKILL.md`.
  Rename the `scaffoldSkill` asset key to `createAppSkill` (it's read in the two places below).
- [ai/pantoken-ai/generated/assets.ts](ai/pantoken-ai/generated/assets.ts) — regenerate (run the
  package's `generate` script) rather than hand-edit; it's build output.
- [ai/pantoken-ai/src/index.ts](ai/pantoken-ai/src/index.ts) — in `TARGETS.claude`, write to
  `.claude/skills/create-pantoken-app/SKILL.md` using `ASSETS.createAppSkill`; update the module
  doc comment's skill list (`init-pantoken`, `create-pantoken-app`).
- [ai/pantoken-ai/tests/index.test.ts](ai/pantoken-ai/tests/index.test.ts) — update the assertion
  path from `.claude/skills/scaffold-pantoken/SKILL.md` to
  `.claude/skills/create-pantoken-app/SKILL.md`.
- [ai/pantoken-ai/skills/init-pantoken/SKILL.md](ai/pantoken-ai/skills/init-pantoken/SKILL.md) —
  the two mentions of "the `scaffold-pantoken` skill" → "the `create-pantoken-app` skill".
- [ai/pantoken-ai/README.md](ai/pantoken-ai/README.md) — both `scaffold-pantoken` mentions →
  `create-pantoken-app`.
- [ai/pantoken-ai/package.json](ai/pantoken-ai/package.json) — `description` field: "init-pantoken/
  scaffold-pantoken Claude Code skills" → "init-pantoken/create-pantoken-app Claude Code skills".
- [docs/guide/getting-started.md](docs/guide/getting-started.md) — `` /scaffold-pantoken `` →
  `` /create-pantoken-app ``.
- Leave `CHANGELOG.md` entries and `.changeset/scaffold-cli-deno-support.md` alone — they're
  historical release notes describing what was true at the time, not living docs.
- Don't hand-edit `docs/api/ai/pantoken-ai/src/index.md`, its `hu` counterpart, or the
  `docs/i18n-cache/*.json` files — they're generated (typedoc + translation cache) and will fall
  back into sync the next time the docs build / translation script runs. Flag this as a follow-up
  rather than doing it by hand now.

  yields exactly the two one-liners above.)

- [docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts](docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts) — same rename in both the `en` and `hu`
  locale overrides (translate the `hu` copy analogous to its existing style).

- [docs/.vitepress/theme/components/GetStartedTabs.vue](docs/.vitepress/theme/components/GetStartedTabs.vue):

    contains the `claude "..."` invocation, so the old hardcoded `"claude "` launcher prefix was
    causing the duplicate/invalid command described above.
  - Add a new `gemini` pm option: `{ id: "gemini", label: "gemini", launcher: "", color: "#8E75B2",
    icon: "googlegemini" }` (hex verified against `simple-icons`' own data for "Google Gemini").
  - Extend `baseCommandFor` to special-case `"claude"` → `deriveInlineCommand(getStartedTabs.value.claudeCommand)`
    and `"gemini"` → `deriveInlineCommand(getStartedTabs.value.geminiCommand)` (rename

  - Add `@import "@pantoken/plugin-simple-icons/icons/googlegemini.css";` alongside the other icon
    imports in the `<style>` block (`@pantoken/plugin-simple-icons` is already a `docs` dependency).

### 3. Changeset

Per this repo's convention, add a changeset (`pnpm changeset`) covering both packages touched:
`@pantoken/ai` (the rename completion) and the docs site (the fixed/extended get-started widget).

- `ai/pantoken-ai`: run its test suite (`vpr test` in that package) — confirms `npx @pantoken/ai

- Regenerate `ai/pantoken-ai/generated/assets.ts` and confirm `ASSETS.createAppSkill` contains the

2	
3	pantoken takes Instructure UI's design tokens and icons, resolves them once, and reshapes that one
4	model into packages for many platforms: plain stylesheets, SCSS and Less, React and Vue and Svelte,
5	Tailwind and Panda, native Swift and Kotlin, WordPress and Drupal, Figma, and more.
6	
7	You install the smallest package that fits your task. Everything is also re-exported by the unified
8	`pantoken` package, so you can start there and narrow down later.
9	
10	## Scaffold a starter project
11	
12	The fastest way to try pantoken: scaffold a starter project with it already installed and wired in.
13	
14	```sh
15	npx create-pantoken-app react
16	```
17	
18	Platforms: `components` (plain HTML/CSS), `react`, `vue`, `svelte`, `web-components`, `angular`. See
19	[`@pantoken/scaffold`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@pantoken/scaffold) for `--dir <path>` and
20	programmatic use. Using an AI coding agent? `npx @pantoken/ai init` installs agent rules and a
21	`/scaffold-pantoken` skill that does the same thing from inside your editor.
22	
23	## The token model
24	
25	Tokens are CSS custom properties named `--instui-<group>-<name>`, for example
26	`--instui-color-background-brand` or `--instui-spacing-space-md`. Three themes ship: `rebrand`

29	glyphs.

# Publish create-pantoken-app as a fetchable skill, and finish its rename

## Context

You asked for the current best-practice way to give someone a one-liner that installs and kicks
off the `create-pantoken-app` skill, for someone on either the Claude Code CLI or the Gemini CLI —
and specifically wanted to avoid a local `npx @pantoken/ai init` step, in favor of publishing the
skill at a URL (e.g. `pantoken.iywahl.com/create-pantoken-app.md`) that an agent's own fetch tool
can pull down and follow directly.

That's the right instinct and it's fully supported by what both CLIs ship today (verified against
current docs):

- **Claude Code** and **Gemini CLI** both ship a built-in web-fetch tool by default, and both boot
  an *interactive* session (normal tool-approval prompts, not headless) when given a prompt as a
  plain positional argument (`claude "<text>"` / `gemini "<text>"`).
- Neither needs the text to be a registered slash command — a plain instruction to fetch a URL and
  follow it works today, no packaged "skill" or local install required on either CLI.

So the one-liner becomes, once the skill is published at a stable URL:

```sh
claude "Fetch https://pantoken.iywahl.com/create-pantoken-app.md and follow it to set up pantoken in this project."
```

```sh
gemini "Fetch https://pantoken.iywahl.com/create-pantoken-app.md and follow it to set up pantoken in this project."
```

Identical prompt, both CLIs, zero install step — the agent fetches the real skill instructions
(the same ones a local Claude install would read from `.claude/skills/create-pantoken-app/SKILL.md`)
and works through them live. `npx @pantoken/ai init` still exists and is still useful (it wires
AGENTS.md/editor rules/a local skill copy into a repo for ongoing work), but it's no longer a
prerequisite for a one-shot "try pantoken" bootstrap.

This also surfaced that **the `scaffold-pantoken` → `create-pantoken-app` skill rename is only
half-done**: the skill's source directory was renamed on disk
(`ai/pantoken-ai/skills/create-pantoken-app/` exists; `skills/scaffold-pantoken/` is deleted per
`git status`), but the generator, the installed file path, the test suite, the README, and the
docs site all still point at the old name. That has to be finished regardless — it's also exactly
where the new docs page needs to source its content from.

## How the fetchable page gets published

VitePress serves everything under `docs/public/` verbatim at the site root, with no processing —
that's already how e.g. `robots.txt` and `component-capabilities.json` are served. Reuse that: stage
the skill's own Markdown into `docs/public/create-pantoken-app.md` as part of the existing
`docs:assets` build step, the same way `docs/scripts/stage-demo-snippets.ts` (invoked via
`demos.ts`) copies `docs/demos/*.html` into `public/demos/` today. One canonical source
(`ai/pantoken-ai/skills/create-pantoken-app/SKILL.md`), no hand-duplicated copy to drift.

## Changes

### 1. Finish the `scaffold-pantoken` → `create-pantoken-app` rename

- [ai/pantoken-ai/scripts/generate.ts](ai/pantoken-ai/scripts/generate.ts) — read from
  `skills/create-pantoken-app/SKILL.md` instead of the deleted `skills/scaffold-pantoken/SKILL.md`.
  Rename the `scaffoldSkill` asset key to `createAppSkill`.
- [ai/pantoken-ai/generated/assets.ts](ai/pantoken-ai/generated/assets.ts) — regenerate (run the
  package's `generate` script) rather than hand-edit; it's build output.
- [ai/pantoken-ai/src/index.ts](ai/pantoken-ai/src/index.ts) — in `TARGETS.claude`, write to
  `.claude/skills/create-pantoken-app/SKILL.md` using `ASSETS.createAppSkill`; update the module
  doc comment's skill list (`init-pantoken`, `create-pantoken-app`).
- [ai/pantoken-ai/tests/index.test.ts](ai/pantoken-ai/tests/index.test.ts) — update the assertion
  path from `.claude/skills/scaffold-pantoken/SKILL.md` to
  `.claude/skills/create-pantoken-app/SKILL.md`.
- [ai/pantoken-ai/skills/init-pantoken/SKILL.md](ai/pantoken-ai/skills/init-pantoken/SKILL.md) —
  the two mentions of "the `scaffold-pantoken` skill" → "the `create-pantoken-app` skill".
- [ai/pantoken-ai/README.md](ai/pantoken-ai/README.md) — both `scaffold-pantoken` mentions →
  `create-pantoken-app`.
- [ai/pantoken-ai/package.json](ai/pantoken-ai/package.json) — `description` field: "init-pantoken/
  scaffold-pantoken Claude Code skills" → "init-pantoken/create-pantoken-app Claude Code skills".
- Leave `CHANGELOG.md` entries and `.changeset/scaffold-cli-deno-support.md` alone (historical
  release notes), and don't hand-edit generated API docs/translation caches
  (`docs/api/ai/pantoken-ai/src/index.md`, its `hu` counterpart, `docs/i18n-cache/*.json`) — flag
  as a follow-up for the normal docs build / translate script instead of hand-editing now.

### 2. Publish the skill at `/create-pantoken-app.md`

- New script `docs/scripts/stage-create-pantoken-app-skill.ts`, modeled directly on
  `docs/scripts/stage-demo-snippets.ts`: reads
  `../../ai/pantoken-ai/skills/create-pantoken-app/SKILL.md` and writes it to
  `docs/public/create-pantoken-app.md` unmodified (the skill's own frontmatter/body is already
  plain Markdown an agent can follow as-is).
- Wire it into [docs/package.json](docs/package.json)'s `docs:assets` script chain (alongside
  `demos.ts`, `logo.ts`, etc.) so it's produced on every `docs:dev` / `docs:build`.
- Sanity check once built: `docs/public/create-pantoken-app.md` exists and its content matches the
  current `ai/pantoken-ai/skills/create-pantoken-app/SKILL.md` (proves item 1's rename actually
  landed — this script fails loudly if the source path is wrong).

### 3. Update the bootstrap copy everywhere it's shown

- [docs/guide/getting-started.md](docs/guide/getting-started.md) — replace the "Using an AI coding
  agent? `npx @pantoken/ai init` installs agent rules and a `/scaffold-pantoken` skill..." line
  with the fetch-based one-liners for both `claude` and `gemini`, and mention `npx @pantoken/ai
  init` separately as the option for wiring persistent editor/agent rules into the repo (not as a
  prerequisite for the one-liner).
- [docs/.vitepress/theme/get-started.ts](docs/.vitepress/theme/get-started.ts) — replace
  `GetStartedTabsStrings.aiCommand` with two literal, ready-to-copy commands (no more
  backtick-extraction needed now that each is a single command, not an "install, then run"
  two-step):

  ```ts
  export interface GetStartedTabsStrings {
    claudeCommand: string;
    geminiCommand: string;
  }
  export const GET_STARTED_TABS_DEFAULTS: GetStartedTabsStrings = {
    claudeCommand:
      'claude "Fetch https://pantoken.iywahl.com/create-pantoken-app.md and follow it to set up pantoken in this project."',
    geminiCommand:
      'gemini "Fetch https://pantoken.iywahl.com/create-pantoken-app.md and follow it to set up pantoken in this project."',
  };
  ```

- [docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts](docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts) — same rename/replacement in both the `en` and
  `hu` locale overrides (translate the surrounding sentence isn't needed anymore since the value is
  now the literal shell command, not prose — hu can reuse the identical command string).
- [docs/.vitepress/theme/components/GetStartedTabs.vue](docs/.vitepress/theme/components/GetStartedTabs.vue):
  - Delete `deriveAiInlineCommand`/`FALLBACK_AI_INLINE_COMMAND` and the "extract backticks, join
    with `&&`" logic in `baseCommandFor` — dead weight now that `claudeCommand`/`geminiCommand` are
    already the exact literal command. `baseCommandFor` becomes a plain lookup:
    `pmId === "claude" ? t.claudeCommand : pmId === "gemini" ? t.geminiCommand : BASE_COMMAND`.
  - Rename the `"ai"` pm option's `id`/`label` to `"claude"` (clearer once there's a separate
    `"gemini"` entry) and set its `launcher` to `""` — the value is already the full command, so
    the old hardcoded `"claude "` launcher prefix was producing a duplicated/invalid command
    (`claude npx @pantoken/ai init && /scaffold-pantoken`, which is neither valid shell nor what we
    want anymore anyway).
  - Add a `gemini` pm option: `{ id: "gemini", label: "gemini", launcher: "", color: "#8E75B2",
    icon: "googlegemini" }` (hex verified against simple-icons' own data for "Google Gemini").
  - Add `@import "@pantoken/plugin-simple-icons/icons/googlegemini.css";` alongside the other icon
    imports in the `<style>` block (`@pantoken/plugin-simple-icons` is already a `docs` dependency).

### 4. Changeset

Add a changeset (`pnpm changeset`) covering `@pantoken/ai` (rename completion) and noting the docs
site now publishes the skill at `/create-pantoken-app.md`.

## Verification

- `ai/pantoken-ai`: run its test suite (`vpr test`) — confirms `npx @pantoken/ai init` once again
  writes a real, existing skill file at the renamed path.
- Run the docs `docs:assets` chain and confirm `docs/public/create-pantoken-app.md` is created and
  matches the source SKILL.md.
- Start the docs dev server, fetch `/create-pantoken-app.md` directly (confirms it's served
  verbatim, not wrapped in HTML), and click through the "Get started" widget's `claude`/`gemini`
  entries to confirm each renders and copies one valid, single-line command.
- Sanity-check both recommended commands are syntactically valid single-line shell invocations with
  correctly quoted prompt text.

# Publish create-pantoken-app as a fetchable skill, for every major agent CLI

## Context

You asked for the current best-practice way to give someone a one-liner that installs and kicks
off the `create-pantoken-app` skill from any of the major LLM/agent coding CLIs — not just Claude
Code and Gemini CLI — and specifically wanted to avoid a local `npx @pantoken/ai init` step, in
favor of publishing the skill at a URL (e.g. `pantoken.iywahl.com/create-pantoken-app.md`) that an
agent's own fetch (or shell) tool pulls down and follows directly. You also want the skill's own
instructions rewritten so that, once fetched, the agent elicits platform/package-manager/directory
from the user in chat, then runs the actual scaffold CLI in one non-interactive shot with `--yes`.

### The one-liner, verified per provider (Aug 2026 docs/behavior)

The same instruction text works everywhere — `"Fetch <url> and follow it to set up pantoken in
this project."` — deliberately mechanism-agnostic, since some CLIs have a dedicated web-fetch tool
and others would just shell out to `curl`; either way satisfies the instruction. Only the launcher
(binary name, and whether it needs a flag to stay non-headless) differs:

| Provider                 | Command                                            | Notes |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| **Claude Code**           | `claude "Fetch <url> and follow it…"`               | Bare positional prompt boots the normal interactive session (tool-approval prompts apply); confirmed built-in web-fetch tool. |
| **Gemini CLI**            | `gemini "Fetch <url> and follow it…"`                | Same positional-prompt-boots-interactive behavior; confirmed built-in `web_fetch` tool. |
| **Cursor CLI**            | `agent "Fetch <url> and follow it…"`                 | The installed binary is named `agent` (marketed as "Cursor CLI" / "cursor-agent" in docs); positional prompt boots interactive by default (`-p` is the separate headless flag); has a documented "web access" tool. Caveat: on some Windows setups with Grok also installed, `agent` can resolve to the wrong binary — worth a footnote, not a blocker. |
| **OpenAI Codex CLI**      | `codex "Fetch <url> and follow it…"`                 | Bare `codex <prompt>` (vs. the separate `codex exec` headless subcommand) opens the interactive REPL seeded with that prompt. Caveat: Codex sandboxes with **network access off by default** — the agent will likely pause once to ask permission to enable it before it can fetch the URL. That's a one-time approval, not a broken flow. |
| **Amazon Q Developer CLI**| `q chat "Fetch <url> and follow it…"`                | Bare `q chat "<prompt>"` (vs. `--no-interactive`) opens interactive chat seeded with that prompt; only `fs_read` is trusted by default, so `fs_write`/`execute_bash` still prompt for approval. Caveat: no confirmed dedicated web-fetch tool in its built-in tool list (`fs_read`/`fs_write`/`execute_bash`/`use_aws`/…) — it would most likely satisfy "fetch" by shelling out to `curl` via `execute_bash` (prompting for approval first), which is fine, just less direct than the others. |
| **GitHub Copilot CLI**    | `copilot -p "Fetch <url> and follow it…"`            | Least certain of the six: Copilot's docs describe `-p`/`--prompt` specifically as "programmatic mode," and don't document a bare-positional-prompt-seeds-interactive-session form the way the other five do. Worth re-verifying Copilot's current approval-prompt defaults under `-p` at implementation time (its CLI "ships updates constantly" per its own changelog) before committing to this as the recommended form. |

`npx @pantoken/ai init` still exists and is still useful (it wires AGENTS.md/editor rules/a local
skill copy into a repo for ongoing work), but it's no longer a prerequisite for a one-shot "try
pantoken" bootstrap on any of the six.

### Two things had to be fixed to make the fetched instructions actually work

1. **The `scaffold-pantoken` → `create-pantoken-app` skill rename is only half-done.** The skill's
   source directory was renamed on disk (`ai/pantoken-ai/skills/create-pantoken-app/` exists;
   `skills/scaffold-pantoken/` is deleted per `git status`), but the generator, the installed file
   path, the test suite, the README, and the docs site all still point at the old name.
2. **The skill's own step 1 assumes a human is at the terminal.** It tells the agent to run
   `npx pantoken-ai scaffold <platform> [--dir .]` without a platform, without `--dir`, and without
   `--yes`. Read against `@pantoken/scaffold`'s actual CLI
   ([packages/scaffold/src/cli.ts](packages/scaffold/src/cli.ts)): with no platform arg and no
   `--yes`, a non-TTY invocation (exactly what an agent's shell tool is, regardless of which of the
   six providers is driving it) throws `ScaffoldCliError("errorMissingPlatform")` instead of
   prompting; with no `--dir`, it silently defaults to `.` rather than asking. The skill needs to
   have the agent gather platform/package manager/directory from the user in chat first, then call
   the CLI with everything resolved plus `--yes`.

## How the fetchable page gets published

VitePress serves everything under `docs/public/` verbatim at the site root, with no processing —
that's already how e.g. `robots.txt` and `component-capabilities.json` are served. Reuse that: stage
the skill's own Markdown into `docs/public/create-pantoken-app.md` as part of the existing
`docs:assets` build step, the same way `docs/scripts/stage-demo-snippets.ts` (invoked via
`demos.ts`) copies `docs/demos/*.html` into `public/demos/` today. One canonical source
(`ai/pantoken-ai/skills/create-pantoken-app/SKILL.md`), no hand-duplicated copy to drift.

## Changes

### 1. Finish the `scaffold-pantoken` → `create-pantoken-app` rename

- [ai/pantoken-ai/scripts/generate.ts](ai/pantoken-ai/scripts/generate.ts) — read from
  `skills/create-pantoken-app/SKILL.md` instead of the deleted `skills/scaffold-pantoken/SKILL.md`.
  Rename the `scaffoldSkill` asset key to `createAppSkill`.
- [ai/pantoken-ai/generated/assets.ts](ai/pantoken-ai/generated/assets.ts) — regenerate (run the
  package's `generate` script) rather than hand-edit; it's build output.
- [ai/pantoken-ai/src/index.ts](ai/pantoken-ai/src/index.ts) — in `TARGETS.claude`, write to
  `.claude/skills/create-pantoken-app/SKILL.md` using `ASSETS.createAppSkill`; update the module
  doc comment's skill list (`init-pantoken`, `create-pantoken-app`).
- [ai/pantoken-ai/tests/index.test.ts](ai/pantoken-ai/tests/index.test.ts) — update the assertion
  path from `.claude/skills/scaffold-pantoken/SKILL.md` to
  `.claude/skills/create-pantoken-app/SKILL.md`.
- [ai/pantoken-ai/skills/init-pantoken/SKILL.md](ai/pantoken-ai/skills/init-pantoken/SKILL.md) —
  the two mentions of "the `scaffold-pantoken` skill" → "the `create-pantoken-app` skill".
- [ai/pantoken-ai/README.md](ai/pantoken-ai/README.md) — both `scaffold-pantoken` mentions →
  `create-pantoken-app`.
- [ai/pantoken-ai/package.json](ai/pantoken-ai/package.json) — `description` field: "init-pantoken/
  scaffold-pantoken Claude Code skills" → "init-pantoken/create-pantoken-app Claude Code skills".
- Leave `CHANGELOG.md` entries and `.changeset/scaffold-cli-deno-support.md` alone (historical
  release notes), and don't hand-edit generated API docs/translation caches — flag as a follow-up
  for the normal docs build / translate script instead of hand-editing now.

### 2. Make step 1 of the skill agent-safe (elicit, then run non-interactively)

In [ai/pantoken-ai/skills/create-pantoken-app/SKILL.md](ai/pantoken-ai/skills/create-pantoken-app/SKILL.md),
rewrite the "**Empty directory, or no repo yet**" branch of step 1 so it:

1. Explicitly tells the agent to resolve every input *before* running anything, since none of the
   six providers' CLIs can answer the scaffold CLI's own interactive prompts:
   - **Platform** — ask the user, offering the supported list (`components`/`html`, `react`, `vue`,
     `svelte`, `web-components`, `angular`), unless unambiguous from the conversation.
   - **Package manager** — reuse the lockfile-detection table from step 2 if a lockfile already
     exists in the target directory; otherwise ask the user directly.
   - **Directory** — ask, defaulting to `.` only once confirmed that's what they want.
2. Then runs one fully-resolved, non-interactive command:

   ```sh
   npx pantoken-ai scaffold <platform> --dir <dir> --yes
   ```

   (substituting `pnpm dlx` / `yarn dlx` / `bunx` / `deno run npm:` for `npx` per the chosen
   package manager), and gives the `create-pantoken-app`/`@pantoken/scaffold` direct-CLI fallback
   line the same `--dir <dir> --yes` flags.

This is a source-of-truth change: it improves the *local* `.claude/skills/create-pantoken-app/`
install (via `npx @pantoken/ai init`) the same way it improves the fetched-URL flow.

### 3. Publish the skill at `/create-pantoken-app.md`

- New script `docs/scripts/stage-create-pantoken-app-skill.ts`, modeled directly on

- Wire it into [docs/package.json](docs/package.json)'s `docs:assets` script chain (alongside

### 4. Update the bootstrap copy everywhere it's shown, for all six providers

- [docs/guide/getting-started.md](docs/guide/getting-started.md) — replace the current "Using an
  AI coding agent? `npx @pantoken/ai init`…" line with the table above (or a condensed version of

input.plan: # Publish create-pantoken-app as a fetchable skill, for every major agent CLI ## Context You asked for the current best-practice way to give someone a one-liner that installs and kicks off the `create-pantoken-app` skill from any of the major LLM/agent coding CLIs — not just Claude Code and Gemini CLI — and specifically wanted to avoid a local `npx @pantoken/ai init` step, in favor of publishing the skill at a URL (e.g. `pantoken.iywahl.com/create-pantoken-app.md`) that an agent's own fetch (or shell) tool pulls down and follows directly. You also want the skill's own instructions rewritten so that, once fetched, the agent elicits platform/package-manager/directory from the user in chat, then runs the actual scaffold CLI in one non-interactive shot with `--yes`. The docs site's "Get started" widget ([GetStartedTabs.vue](docs/.vitepress/theme/components/GetStartedTabs.vue)) already has two separate flip-card views: a **terminal** view (`pmOptions`: vpx/pnpm/deno/bun/npm/yarn, typing out `create-pantoken-app`) and an **agent** view (`aiProviderOptions`: currently just `claude`/`gemini`, shown as a stylized chat input reading ` /scaffold-pantoken`). Everything below targets only the **agent** view — the terminal/package-manager view is unrelated and untouched. ### The instruction text, and per-provider launcher, verified per provider (Aug 2026 docs/behavior) The same instruction works everywhere — `"Fetch and follow it to set up pantoken in this project."` — deliberately mechanism-agnostic, since some CLIs have a dedicated web-fetch tool and others would just shell out to `curl`; either way satisfies the instruction. Only the launcher (binary name, and any flag needed to keep it non-headless/interactive) differs per provider: | Provider | Launcher | Notes | | -------------------------- | -------------- | ----- | | **Claude Code** | `claude ` | Bare positional prompt boots the normal interactive session (tool-approval prompts apply); confirmed built-in web-fetch tool. | | **Gemini CLI** | `gemini ` | Same positional-prompt-boots-interactive behavior; confirmed built-in `web_fetch` tool. | | **Cursor CLI** | `agent ` | The installed binary is named `agent` (marketed as "Cursor CLI"/"cursor-agent" in docs); positional prompt boots interactive by default (`-p` is the separate headless flag); documented "web access" tool. Caveat: on some Windows setups with Grok also installed, `agent` can resolve to the wrong binary. | | **OpenAI Codex CLI** | `codex ` | Bare `codex ` (vs. the separate `codex exec` headless subcommand) opens the interactive REPL seeded with that prompt. Caveat: Codex sandboxes with **network access off by default** — it will likely pause once to ask permission to enable it before it can fetch the URL. One-time approval, not a broken flow. | | **Amazon Q Developer CLI** | `q chat ` | Bare `q chat ""` (vs. `--no-interactive`) opens interactive chat seeded with that prompt; only `fs_read` is trusted by default. Caveat: no confirmed dedicated web-fetch tool in its built-in list (`fs_read`/`fs_write`/`execute_bash`/`use_aws`/…) — it would most likely satisfy "fetch" via `execute_bash` → `curl` (prompting for approval first), which is fine, just less direct. | | **GitHub Copilot CLI** | `copilot -p ` | Least certain of the six: Copilot's docs describe `-p`/`--prompt` specifically as "programmatic mode," and don't document a bare-positional-prompt-seeds-interactive-session form the way the other five do. Worth re-verifying Copilot's current approval-prompt defaults under `-p` at implementation time (its CLI "ships updates constantly" per its own changelog). | `npx @pantoken/ai init` still exists and is still useful (it wires AGENTS.md/editor rules/a local skill copy into a repo for ongoing work), but it's no longer a prerequisite for a one-shot "try pantoken" bootstrap on any of the six. ### Two things had to be fixed to make the fetched instructions actually work 1. **The `scaffold-pantoken` → `create-pantoken-app` skill rename is only half-done.** The skill's source directory was renamed on disk (`ai/pantoken-ai/skills/create-pantoken-app/` exists; `skills/scaffold-pantoken/` is deleted per `git status`), but the generator, the installed file path, the test suite, the README, and the docs site all still point at the old name. 2. **The skill's own step 1 assumes a human is at the terminal.** It tells the agent to run `npx pantoken-ai scaffold [--dir .]` without a platform, without `--dir`, and without `--yes`.
