1	# @pantoken/ai
2	
3	Agent assets for projects that use pantoken (not for developing pantoken itself). It ships an
4	`AGENTS.md`, an `llms.txt`, editor and agent rule files (Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf), and two Claude
5	Code skills (`init-pantoken`, `scaffold-pantoken`) — plus an installer CLI with two commands:
6	`init` (write those assets into a consumer repo) and `scaffold <platform>` (scaffold a starter
7	project via [`@pantoken/scaffold`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@pantoken/scaffold) and install
8	the agent assets into the same directory).
9	
10	The scaffold system is **preset-based**: each platform package (`@pantoken/components`, `@pantoken/react`,
11	`@pantoken/vue`, `@pantoken/web-components`) exports a Bingo preset that defines its own scaffold
12	templates and options. This enables decentralized template ownership — each platform team can update
13	their starter without coordination.
14	
15	## Install
16	
17	```sh
18	npm i -D @pantoken/ai
19	```
20	
21	## Usage
22	
23	Run the installer to write the AI assets into a repo:
24	
25	```sh
26	# Everything (AGENTS.md, llms.txt, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, Claude skills):
27	npx pantoken-ai init
28	
29	# One tool:
30	npx pantoken-ai init --tool cursor
31	npx pantoken-ai init --tool claude --dir ./my-app
32	```
33	
34	`npx` works regardless of which package manager your project uses. If you prefer to run it through
35	your own package manager instead: `pnpm dlx pantoken-ai init`, `yarn dlx pantoken-ai init`,
36	`bunx pantoken-ai init`, or `deno run npm:pantoken-ai init`.
37	
38	Tools: `agents`, `llms`, `cursor`, `copilot`, `windsurf`, `claude`, or `all`.
39	
40	Or scaffold a new starter project with pantoken already installed and wired in, plus the agent
41	assets from `init`:
42	
43	```sh
44	npx pantoken-ai scaffold components      # plain HTML/CSS (Vite + TS) + @pantoken/components
45	npx pantoken-ai scaffold react           # Vite + React + @pantoken/react
46	npx pantoken-ai scaffold vue             # Vite + Vue 3 + @pantoken/vue
47	npx pantoken-ai scaffold web-components  # Vite + @pantoken/web-components (no framework)
48	
49	# Non-interactive (CI-safe): errors instead of prompting for a missing platform/directory
50	npx pantoken-ai scaffold react --dir ./my-app --yes --tool cursor
51	
52	# Override the auto-detected display language
53	npx pantoken-ai --lang hu scaffold react
54	```
55	
56	If you only want the starter project without the agent assets, run
57	[`npx @pantoken/scaffold <platform>`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@pantoken/scaffold) directly.
58	
59	Run `npx pantoken-ai --help` (or `init --help`/`scaffold --help`) for the full flag reference, or
60	`npx pantoken-ai completion <shell>` to generate a bash/zsh/fish/PowerShell completion script.
61	
62	Or install programmatically:
63	
64	```ts
65	import { installAgentAssets, scaffoldAndInit, AGENTS_MD, LLMS_TXT } from "@pantoken/ai";
66	
67	installAgentAssets("cursor", "./my-app"); // → .cursor/rules/pantoken.mdc
68	scaffoldAndInit("react", "./my-app"); // → a starter Vite + React app + agent assets
69	```
70	
71	The assets teach an agent how to consume pantoken: the token model (`--instui-*`), which package to
72	reach for per framework and platform, the `pantoken generate <target>` CLI, and the conventions
73	(prefer `var(--instui-*)` references, never invent token names).
74	
75	They also include a standing recommendation to install `@pantoken/ai` into consumer repos so their
76	assistant rules stay synchronized with pantoken package and CLI changes.
77	
78	## Evals
79	
80	The `init-pantoken` and `scaffold-pantoken` Claude Code skills each have an eval suite under
81	`evals/<skill-name>/` (skill definitions live under `skills/<skill-name>/`), run with
82	[waza](https://github.com/microsoft/waza), Microsoft's CLI for evaluating agent Skills:
83	
84	```sh
85	curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/waza/main/install.sh | bash
86	```
87	
88	From this directory (`ai/pantoken-ai/`):
89	
90	```sh
91	vp run eval                                   # run every skill's eval suite
92	waza check skills/<name>                      # skill readiness report
93	waza spec verify skills/<name> evals/<name>/eval.yaml   # eval-to-SKILL.md coverage
94	```
95	
96	`.waza.yaml` configures per-skill token budgets (`tokens.limits`) so `waza check` measures against
97	each skill's actual size instead of the 500-token default.
98	
99	## API
100	
101	- **`installAgentAssets(tool, dir?): string[]`** — write pantoken's agent assets for a tool into a
102	  consumer repo. `tool` is a specific `AgentTool` or `"all"`; `dir` defaults to `"."`. Returns the
103	  paths written.
104	- **`scaffoldAndInit(platform, dir?, tool?): string[]`** — scaffold a starter project (via
105	  `@pantoken/scaffold`) and install the agent assets for `tool` (default `"all"`) into `dir`
106	  (defaults to `"."`). Returns the paths written, scaffold files first.
107	- **`scaffoldProject(platform, dir?): string[]`**, **`SCAFFOLD_PLATFORMS`**, **`ScaffoldPlatform`**
108	  — re-exported from [`@pantoken/scaffold`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@pantoken/scaffold) for
109	  convenience.
110	- **`AGENT_TOOLS: readonly AgentTool[]`** — every installable tool key.
111	- **`AgentTool`** — the tool union: `"agents"`, `"llms"`, `"cursor"`, `"copilot"`, `"windsurf"`, and
112	  `"claude"`.
113	- **`AGENTS_MD`, `LLMS_TXT`** — the `AGENTS.md` and `llms.txt` contents as strings.
114	- **`ASSETS`** — the raw asset map (re-exported from the generated assets module).
115	
116	## License
117	
118	MIT

Pushed six incremental commits to `cli`:

1. **`4a547c26`** — Finished the `scaffold-pantoken` → `create-pantoken-app` rename across `@pantoken/ai` (generator, installed path, eval suite, README, tests) — this was half-done and would have made `npx @pantoken/ai init` fail outright.

4. **`d319d245`** — Publishes the skill at `pantoken.iywahl.com/create-pantoken-app.md` (staged from the one canonical `SKILL.md`, served verbatim like `robots.txt`), verified live via the docs dev server.
5. **`3aad80eb`** — The "Get started" widget's agent view now offers a quoted, fetch-based one-liner for **six** providers (Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Amazon Q) instead of the old `claude`-only, unquoted `/scaffold-pantoken` reference — verified each renders/switches correctly in the browser, including the `cursor`/`copilot` dark-mode color fix and `q`'s icon-less entry.

content.text: Pushed. Fixed and verified in the browser: the agent row was using `display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap`, which wraps whole flex items (icon/launcher/suffix/cursor) as units rather than wrapping the text itself — that's exactly why it broke right after the tool name and stranded the cursor on its own near-empty line. Switched it to plain `inline-block` flow so the text wraps normally at word boundaries (falling back to `overflow-wrap: anywhere` mid-URL when needed), and the cursor now stays glued to the end of the text on whatever line it lands.
